[b]Death in the Family[/b]

P.K Sujibhan was dead. He had served Dakshina faithfully, winning the first Consul Elections of 1957, and getting re-elected every year until his death, an impressive sixty-nine approval elections won, and 17 Consul elections won. The most recent approval elections in 2026 were the closest in decades, with it seeming that the iron fist the Dakshinese Unity Party once held was fading, and with Sujibhan's death it's anticipated that the Unity Party will fall with him. In the meantime. In his place, Consul election runner-up Poorattathi L. will assume office, running as a Marxist Party member from the more-developed state of Sargadesh.

Poorattathi prior to the election promised a similar economic platform to that utilized by the Marxist Party of Sargadesh, which saw the poverty-stricken coastline transform itself into the most developed and educated in all of Dakshina. To Dakshinese partners abroad, Poorattathi has promised little shift in its foreign policies from that of the later Sujibhan regime, striving for what will best protect and strengthen Dakshina and the Dakshinese people, with an emphasis on the Talittukal (plebian) wealth class.

To many in Dakshina, Poorattathi's election marks a sign of hope. He comes from a poorer family, not the usual Vaiciya aristocrat wanting more stagnant Unity Party policies, but to replicate the groundbreaking change in Sargadesh the Marxist Party must fight a crushing uphill battle. 

Even with the death of their political pillar, the Unity Party's immense political machine is what allowed their unpopular policies to succeed through the democratic process in the past. Time will tell if the Marxist Party is successful in their endeavors, or if Poorattathi is merely ousted within the year.

[b]NTV Daily News[/b]

[i]*a 15 second long intro flashes onto TV screens, before a young man, around 22, adjusts his tie and folds his hands on a lectern*[/i]

Good evening, my name is Hassan Nur and I am your moderator for tonights news.

[spoiler=Administrative Unification]

[i]*a video of acting Premier Arlan Vos signing documens is shown*[/i]
Today marks a historic turning point for our country. After thirty-two years of fragmentation, all administrative regions of Tirakan have officially been unified under one central government for the first time since the outbreak of the civil war in 1995. The transition documents were finalized earlier this morning, confirming the reintegration of former RU, CA and HL territories into a single national administration seated in Naerim. This marks the end of the short-lived transitional governance era.

[i]*a video of cars on the N2 highway blends in*[/i]
With the administrative reunification completed, the nationwide infrastructure and reconstruction programs have accelerated significantly. According to the Ministry of Infrastructure, highway corridors linking the former front-line regions to Naerim are ahead of schedule, and more than sixty percent of damaged rail lines have been restored to operational capacity. Port reconstruction in Marrin and the northern harbors continues at an intensive pace, supported by newly procured equipment and foreign engineering partnerships.

Power grid stabilization has also seen notable progress, with the first unified national energy map now being prepared to reconnect the eastern and western grids by the end of the year. Water networks, hospitals, and public service centers in former conflict zones are being opened one after another, some of them for the first time in decades. The Ministry emphasized that reconstruction teams have been deployed continuously, and thousands of newly trained workers from Naerims vocational programs have joined the effort.

Minister of Infrastructure, Hassan Al-Sherbir, states that... [i]*a video of Hassan Al-Sherbir responding to a reporters question*[/i] ...the governments priority is to restore equal living standards across all regions, ensuring that basic services, transport access, and economic opportunities reach every province. [i]*the video fades out*[/i] Further updates on the nationwide reconstruction agenda will be released over the coming weeks as assessments conclude.

[/spoiler]

[spoiler=Industrial Growth]
Let us continue, with the new government reports,showing strong upward momentum across both new and traditional industries. Major investment rounds have been finalized in Naerims semiconductor sector, AI research clusters, drone manufacturing facilities and the rapidly expanding computing industry. Acting Premier Arlan Vos describes these high-tech fields, as the core engines of Tirakans long-term growth strategy.

At the same time, legacy sectors, including copper and iron production, rare-earth extraction, defense manufacturing, national logistics hubs and the gas industry, are receiving substantial reinvestment to restore full capacity after decades of disruption. Officials say these combined developments are already reflected in national indicators: industrial output has risen for three consecutive quarters, GDP recovery is outpacing earlier forecasts, and consumer confidence has reached its highest level since before the war.

According to the Ministry of Commerce, retail activity, household spending and small-business formation are all trending positively, signaling that the populations economic mood is improving significantly as stability returns. Consumer prices are expected to consecutively meet new lows over the next years. Capital manager, Paul Markerson, advices families to invest their money into the home industry today, and expect large cashouts in a decade.
[/spoiler]

[spoiler=Valdderan Relations]
Turning to regional diplomacy, the Minister of Foreign Relations, Zayllah bin Abyan commented today on the recent end of hostilities in [nation]Valddera[/nation]. In an interview recorded earlier, he welcomed the development as a major step toward restoring long-term stability in East Shamat. We now bring you a short excerpt from that conversation.

[i]*The interview blends in*[/i]

For Tirakan, the conclusion of the conflict in Valddera is a positive and encouraging signal. Stability is the foundation on which all states in East Shamat should depend, but mostly don't, and we are relieved to see a reduction of armed tensions so close to our shared border.
Let me be clear: we are not merely looking for resumed trade or standard diplomatic exchanges. Tirakan and Valddera are neighboring lands, shaped by geography, history, and the realities of living side-by-side. Our goal is long-term, brotherly relations based on mutual respect, predictable cooperation and a shared vision for regional security.
As Valddera begins rebuilding, Greater Tirakan will do anything in it's might to improve it's hurt relations with the country. Public measure on this regard, will follow soon.

[i]*Hassan fades in once again*[/i]
The Ministry reports that they wish for further bilateral talks, in the coming weeks as both countries adjust to the new post-conflict landscape.
[/spoiler]

[spoiler=The Corridor]
To follow up, one of the governments flagship diplomatic and economic initiatives is moving rapidly toward realization. The proposed Tirakan-Vespurias Trade Corridor, long described as the signature project of both the Minister of Economics and the Minister of Foreign Relations, has now secured preliminary approval from eleven of the fourteen invited nations. Officials emphasize that this level of early alignment is unprecedented for a multistate agreement of this scale.

[i]*multiple videos of Acting Premier Arlan Vos shaking hands fade in one after another*[/i]

According to the Ministry, participating governments have already confirmed their readiness to streamline customs procedures and join a shared security framework designed to keep trade routes stable and protected. The Corridor is expected to form a continuous commercial chain across East Shamat, linking markets, ports and industrial centers in a way that analysts say could reshape regional economics for decades, especially for the biggest beneficiary, ourselves, Great Tirakan.

While the formal signing of the treaty has not yet occurred, diplomatic sources report that most technical negotiations have been concluded, and only final legal formatting remains. The government expects the agreement to enter its signature phase in the coming months. As senior official Abin bin Babin stated today, The Corridor is no longer an idea on paper, it is an unstoppable force becoming reality, and it will define Tirakans role in the region.
[/spoiler]

[spoiler=Increased Trade]
[i]*Hassan clears his throat as a picture of the Marrin cargo mega port blends in*[/i]
Economic analysts also report renewed strength in Tirakans external trade. Shipments to our closest partners, particularly [nation]Vespurias[/nation], [nation]Nordiheim[/nation], and since very recently [nation]Valodya[/nation], have increased steadily over the past two quarters. The Ministry of Commerce attributes this rise to restored infrastructure, higher industrial output, and the reopening of northern and coastal logistics routes previously disrupted by the conflict.

Export volumes of refined gas, copper products, manufactured goods and high-value components have all shown significant recovery. In parallel, import channels for machinery, electronics, and specialty materials have stabilized, improving supply consistency for domestic industries.

These trends are already being felt by households. Consumer prices, which had remained elevated throughout the later years of the civil war, are now showing a clear downward shift. Lower logistics costs, improved port efficiency, and recovered market confidence are cited as key drivers. Officials state that, if current patterns continue, Tirakan may enter its first sustained period of price normalization in more than a decade.

[i]*a map of Tirakans current and potential future trade routes fades in*[/i]

The Tirakan-Vespurias corridor will play an essential role in positioning Tirakan as a future trade giant, says Arlan Vos, after infrastructure and public service will have been re-constructed fully. Plans to for a second corridor and trade agreements reaching across the whole world, have been made public. In ambiton of the acting premier himself, a large sum of cargo ships are being restructured to be able to refuel without stopping, through steady following military vessels. This will allow for not only a new trade route, never having existed before, to be created, but as well as record time shipping from Elseyr to East Shamat. 
[/spoiler]

[spoiler=Nuclear Progression]
Lastly, Ladies and Gentlemen, we bring news in science and energy news. Yesterday evening, the Naerim Strategic Research Authority [i](NSRA)[/i] has released an update on Tirakans national nuclear energy program. According to the newest projections, construction, testing and final calibration of the civilian reactor network remain on schedule, even though full operational readiness is given, the programs finalization expected in early 2030, for currently unknown reasons. The program is described as one of the countrys most technically ambitious post-war undertakings, aimed at securing long-term energy independence and reducing reliance on fossil fuels.

*the up and running reactor is shown from far away in a video running next to Hassan*

Government officials reiterated today that the program is strictly civilian in nature. In response to questions from foreign reporters, the government reaffirmed that Greater Tirakan has no intention of producing nuclear warheads or pursuing a weapons program, emphasizing that all activity remains under regulatory oversight of the government themselves.
Jiosef Al-Izzaham, vice-president of the NSRA also added that the reactors will play a central role in stabilizing the national grid, supporting industrial expansion, and ensuring affordable electricity for consumers as reconstruction continues. There is no supposed need of worry.
[/spoiler]

That concludes todays national update. As Tirakan continues rebuilding and celebrating its independence, we will keep bringing you the latest developments from across the country! Thank you for watching NTV. We wish you a safe and peaceful evening!

[i]*a long outro ends the program*[/i]

[spoiler=2027 World Expo Entry Submission] [i]The government of the Confederacy of Lamandica would like to formally acknowledge the government of Greater Tirakan as the sole government in the land that Naerim-City resides power over. Additionally, the Lamandican government would like to thank Tirakan for giving them this opportunity to participate in the 2027 World Expo, and will send a delegation to Tirakan as an act of goodwill between the two nations.[/i]

[b]THE LAMANDICAN SMART HIGHWAY (Theme: Sustainability)[/b]

Motorways have played a crucial role in the modern development of Lamandica and the world. These limited access highways help connect cities and different regions with each other. Lamandica is home to some of the world's first highways, such as the Encrastle Urban Parkway in Taultion. However, these highways cause pollution, noise, and overall, could be quite ugly. However, Lamandica is in the process of minimizing the impacts of these highways, with what they call, the Smart Highway. The first one in Lamandica opened up in 2019 when a section of L.H. 1727 was upgraded north of Taultion. And now, with the success of that portion of highway, Lamandica wants to showcase the benefits of the Smart Highway to the world.

At Lamandicas exhibit, they hope to have a near 15,000 square feet of floorspace. A diorama, where expressways criss-cross around a city's downtown, lined by homes, business, and industrial areas. Industrial areas, at least in Lamandica, were where the highways originally cut through, but the factories have been replaced by homes over time. Homes, where property values are always considerably less than the rest of the city and where people are fleeing. However, this is where Lamandicas smart highway comes in. These expressways choking the city centre are all made out of recycled materials. Plastic, asphalt, and rubber all smelted together to create a porous road surface, small enough for cars to not be impacted, but large enough for water to drain. Highway overpasses dotted with solar panels, with more dashed in the rows of trees lining the highway. Not only for decoration, but also to absorb carbon dioxide from the highway. The diorama also showcases sensors to detect heavy traffic and possible collisions. The Lamandican Smart Highway exhibit hopes to showcase sustainable, less environmentally damaging highway infrastructure. The exhibit will also include remote-controlled cars on a set path manned by a team of scientists to put the highways to the test.

Also, the rest of the diorama will also act as a side exhibit to demonstrate a vision for the City of the Future. Parts of the highways would be set underground, with caps being built over them, forming tunnels. Many of these tunnels will have parks and mixed-use dense zoning on top of them. Green spaces will be spread throughout the city for recreational use. Parking would be minimalized, with large park structures taking less floorspace and would be in mainly industrial areas with lifts connecting them to downtown. Instead of using cars, citizens would be encouraged to use public transportation with frequent stops connecting nearly every corner of the city. However, and perhaps most importantly, it showcases the idea of a Ten-Minute City. A Ten-Minute City is where citizens can enjoy a walkable and bike-friendly neighborhood, with all amenities such as education, healthcare, food, etc. within ten minutes from any given location.

Overall, Lamandicas diorama hopes to show sustainability for future development in cities and roadway infrastructure environmentally safe for decades to come.[/spoiler]
